pull.title: fix(anthropic-oauth): stop a dead store masking a working credential (6.43.0)
pull.body:
## Why

The `anthropic_oauth` provider had **never served a single request** on the reporter's machine: `requests.db` held 0 rows for it against 11,122 for `chatgpt_oauth`, and `/admin/api/anthropic-oauth/sources` reported `windows.observed=false` — no Anthropic response had ever carried a rate-limit header.

Four reported symptoms ("cred refresh not working", "importing cred from `.claude` not working properly", "code errors", "no way to fix it from the dashboard") turned out to be four separate defects stacked on one root cause.

## B1–B11 → file:line

| | Severity | What was wrong | Fixed in |
|---|---|---|---|
| **B1** | BLOCKER | `load_tokens()` picked the managed store on `has_access_token` alone, so a token that expired days ago permanently masked a healthy `~/.claude` credential | `providers/anthropic_oauth/credentials.py` — `credential_viability()`, `load_tokens()`, `quarantine_managed_store()` |
| **B2** | BLOCKER | every refresh failure, 429 included, said "sign in again" | `credentials.py` — `AnthropicOAuthRefreshRejected` / `AnthropicOAuthRefreshUnavailable`, `classify_refresh_failure()`, `DEFINITIVE_REFRESH_STATUSES` |
| **B3** | HIGH | the running provider cached the credential for the process lifetime | `providers/anthropic_oauth/auth.py` — `_store_stamp()`, `current_tokens()`, `invalidate()` |
| **B4** | HIGH | the dashboard discarded `credential_reference` and gave no next step | `api/admin_static/admin.js` — `fillAnthropicOAuthFields()`, "Apply settings to activate the provider." |
| **B5** | HIGH | no dashboard refresh, no disconnect | `api/admin_routes.py` — `anthropic_oauth_refresh`, `anthropic_oauth_disconnect`; `admin.js` — "Refresh now", "Disconnect" |
| **B6** | MEDIUM | the CLI raised raw tracebacks; no `--help` | `providers/anthropic_oauth/cli.py` (rewritten) |
| **B7** | MEDIUM | the token-endpoint request did not match Claude Code's | `constants.py`, `credentials.py` — `token_endpoint_headers()`, `_refresh_payload()`, `OAUTH_REFRESH_SCOPES` |
| **B8** | MEDIUM | a pasted callback URL was sent as the code | `providers/anthropic_oauth/oauth_login.py` — `split_pasted_code()` |
| **B9** | LOW | the discovery log carried no status code | `providers/runtime/validation.py` — `safe_message` marker |
| **B10** | LOW | nothing warned that the refresh token itself was dead | `credential_viability()`; `admin.js` — "Refresh token expired" |
| **B11** | INFO | verified-correct, left alone | wire constants, `_expiry_seconds`, `_atomic_write_private_json`, single-flight refresh, `require_loopback_admin`, `sdk-cli` in the entrypoint set, the `free_claude_code` shims |

Plus the binding decisions: the **loopback callback sign-in** (`providers/anthropic_oauth/loopback.py`, `admin_routes.py` `loopback/{initiate,status}`) alongside the paste flow, the **macOS keychain** message on `darwin`, and quarantine-by-rename rather than delete.

### On decision 5 — no special-casing

Transient refresh failures get **no OAuth-specific retry loop**. `AnthropicOAuthProvider._classify_credential_failure` maps them onto the *existing* `FailureKind`s and the existing machinery does the rest:

| Token-endpoint result | `FailureKind` | Retryable | Wire type | Benches the model |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 429 | `RATE_LIMIT` | yes, honours `Retry-After` | `rate_limit_error` | no |
| 5xx / transport | `OVERLOADED` | yes | `overloaded_error` | yes |
| 400/401/403 + OAuth body | `AUTHENTICATION` | no | `authentication_error` | yes |
| no credential | `UNAVAILABLE` | no | `api_error` | no |

**No `FailureKind` was added**, so the three wire tables, the constants mirror and the enumerating tests are untouched. The override is threaded into *both* `execute_with_retry` and `classify_provider_failure` via a new `set_failure_override()` setter, matching the `set_auth_retry`/`set_response_observer` house pattern.

## Research pass — Claude Code 2.1.260

Read from `~/.local/share/claude/versions/2.1.260` (PE32+ Bun bundle, **217,771,680 bytes**, `VERSION:"2.1.260"`, `BUILD_TIME:"2026-09-03T19:41:35Z"`, `GIT_SHA:"e51f681183f733dbe9a81bf35921c786ee26dbc6"`). Bundled Anthropic TS SDK `var ne="0.112.1"`. Every constant in `constants.py` now cites a 2.1.260 offset and a quoted snippet; the pre-6.43.0 file cited 2.1.258 offsets, one of which described a request shape no Claude Code login path makes.

### Token endpoint

`$U` (offset 182768825) and `EAn` (offset 182768091) both post with `{headers:{"Content-Type":"application/json"},timeout:30000}` and nothing else; `$U`'s body carries `scope:(Array.isArray(n)&&n.length?n:p8).join(" ")`.

| | before | after | source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Content-Type` | `application/json` | unchanged | offset 182768825 |
| `anthropic-beta` | `oauth-2025-04-20` | **removed** | not in `$U`/`EAn`; it is the SDK's *`userOAuthProvider`* at offset 180228922, a path Claude Code's login never takes |
| `User-Agent` | `anthropic` | `claude-cli/2.1.260 (external, cli)` | offset 182853338 + live evidence below |
| refresh `scope` | *absent* | `p8` (5 scopes, no `org:create_api_key`) | offset 180721391 |

The `User-Agent` is the one place the binary is not taken literally, and the live test is why: Claude Code sets no *explicit* UA but its HTTP client supplies one, and sending none is answered by a non-JSON `403` at the edge.

### `/v1/messages` with an OAuth bearer

`iF` (offset 186629277) builds `defaultHeaders` `{"x-app": ht()?"cli-bg":"cli", "User-Agent": zR(), "X-Claude-Code-Session-Id": …}` with `dangerouslyAllowBrowser:!0`; the SDK's `buildHeaders` (offset 180347171) adds `Accept`, `anthropic-version: 2023-06-01`, `anthropic-dangerous-direct-browser-access`, `Authorization: Bearer` (never `x-api-key` when `apiKey===null`) and the `X-Stainless-*` block (`ki()`, offset 180207351). `anthropic-beta` comes from `Dre()` (offset 182339086), which pushes `oauth-2025-04-20` on the OAuth branch and `claude-code-20250219` off haiku.

| header | MCC 6.43.0 |
|---|---|
| `Authorization: Bearer` | sent (never `x-api-key`) |
| `anthropic-version` | client's, else `2023-06-01` |
| `anthropic-beta` | floor `oauth-2025-04-20,claude-code-20250219` ∪ client's, allow-listed |
| `anthropic-dangerous-direct-browser-access` | `true` |
| `x-app` | client's, else `cli` |
| `user-agent` | client's, else `claude-cli/2.1.260 (external, cli)` |
| **`accept: application/json`** | **added in this PR** |
| `X-Stainless-*` (8), `X-Claude-Code-Session-Id` | **deliberately not sent** |

The two omissions are documented in `constants.CLAUDE_CODE_HEADERS_NOT_MIRRORED` rather than silently skipped. They describe the JavaScript runtime that built the request (`X-Stainless-Lang: js`, `X-Stainless-Runtime: node`, an OS, an arch) and the client's own session id. MCC is Python and is not that session; emitting them would manufacture claims, which this provider's header table and `core/client_fingerprint.py` both explicitly forbid. Neither gates anything — the OAuth gate is `anthropic-beta: oauth-2025-04-20` and the credential gate is `Authorization`, and MCC sends both. Two registry betas new in 2.1.260 were added to the allow-list (`auto-mode-classifier-2026-07-16`, `thinking-display-updates-2026-08-18`).

## Consented live test

> **8. yes**

to

> **8. May I run the consented live test in (h)?** *Recommendation: yes* — it is at most 3 requests on your own subscription and it is the only way to distinguish "the refresh token is expired" from "the header set is rejected", which changes which of B2/B7 is the real blocker for *your* credential.

No token value was printed, logged or committed.

**Request 1** — Claude Code's exact refresh shape (`Content-Type` only), managed store's refresh token, on-the-wire UA `Python-urllib/3.13` → **HTTP 403, 17-byte non-JSON body.** Not an OAuth error shape; an edge block that never reached the OAuth handler.

**Request 2** — same refresh token, MCC 6.42.1's header set via httpx → **HTTP 429**, `server: cloudflare`, `cf-ray: a35ba3890f87d0db-SOF`:

```json
{"error": {"type": "rate_limit_error", "message": "Rate limited. Please try again later."}}
```

**→ The refresh token is alive. It is rate-limited. B2 was the blocker; B1 made it permanent; B7 was not the blocker.** MCC 6.42.1 turned that 429 into "Sign in again with `mcc-anthropic-oauth-login`" — advice that would have rotated a working refresh token away.

**Request 3** — one prompt through a scratch MCC (`127.0.0.1:8199`, scratch `MCC_CONFIG_DIR` with **no** managed store, stopped by exact PID). The scratch log's first lines:

```
WARNING  Claude subscription credential: using claude-code (access token still valid); skipped mcc (absent)
INFO     Claude subscription gate: marker=cli ua_entrypoint=cli x_app=cli ua_version=2.1.260 agreed=True admitted=True enforced=True
```

and Anthropic answered `HTTP 429 {"type":"error","error":{"type":"rate_limit_error"},"request_id":"req_011Cei9GZC9yoPGobJfLW4NS"}`, producing the **first ever `provider='anthropic_oauth'` row** in a request log on this machine:

| `provider` | `requested_model` | `error_kind` | `key_label` | `harness` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `anthropic_oauth` | `anthropic_oauth/claude-sonnet-4-6` | `rate_limit` | `max · claude-code` | `claude` |

`key_label = max · claude-code` **is B1's fix serving traffic.** Anthropic accepted the credential and the header set and returned a first-class API response with its own `request_id` — a rejected credential answers 401, an unentitled beta answers 400. A `200` was not reachable because the account is inside a rate-limit window; everything up to Anthropic's acceptance is proven, the completion itself is not.

### Request budget — one overrun, stated plainly

| # | Upstream calls | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 | 403 |
| 2 | 1 | 429 |
| 3 | **3** | 429 × 3 |
| | **5 total** | vs. a consented **3** |

I sent one prompt; MCC's own retry ladder turned it into three upstream attempts ~60 s apart before giving up. That is the ladder behaving correctly for a 429 and a budgeting mistake on my part. All three were refused at Anthropic's rate limiter before any inference ran, so no tokens were billed (no `usage` returned), and requests 1–2 bill nothing — but the number was 5, not 3.

### The real credential files were not modified

Neither refresh succeeded, so no refresh token rotated and the sanctioned write-back was never needed. Verified by hash afterwards: `~/.fcc/anthropic_oauth.json` (`9754…`, mtime 2026-09-01 02:15:15Z) and `~/.claude/.credentials.json` (`d692…`, mtime 2026-09-04 04:42:37Z) are byte-identical to the copies taken before the test. No `.bak-*` and no `.dead-*` were created in the real `~/.fcc`. The scratch credential copies were deleted.

## For this operator

**Nothing to do.** Upgrading is the whole fix: the stale `~/.fcc/anthropic_oauth.json` stops masking the healthy `~/.claude` credential, so the provider starts working on the fallback, and the next 429 is reported as a rate limit rather than as a dead credential.

## Tests

`tests/providers/test_anthropic_oauth_selection.py` (22), `test_oauth_refresh_parity.py` (17), `test_anthropic_oauth_failure_ladder.py` (21), `test_anthropic_oauth_loopback.py` (19), `test_discovery_failure_messages.py` (5), `tests/cli/test_anthropic_oauth_login_cli.py` (8), `tests/api/test_admin_anthropic_oauth_controls.py` (11), plus rewritten wire assertions.

`test_anthropic_and_chatgpt_oauth_agree_on_refresh_failure_classes` pins both providers' `DEFINITIVE_REFRESH_STATUSES` together so the two cannot drift apart again.

**9,316 passed, 48 skipped** (full suite) + **219 passed** (jsdom, `-n0`). `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `ty` all clean. No `# type: ignore`. Contract tests green — one import-boundary exception added for `admin_routes -> anthropic_oauth.loopback`, matching the four that already exist for this provider.

## Docs

`docs/ANTHROPIC-SUBSCRIPTION.md` (+157: the selection rule, the two failure classes, quarantine, the buttons, both sign-in flows, `--help`, the token-endpoint table), `docs/USAGE.md` (the dashboard flow, and that no restart is needed), `docs/CLAUDE-CODE-CONFIG.md` (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` + the macOS keychain caveat), and `constants.py`'s provenance block.

There is no `CHANGELOG.md` in this repo — the user-visible summary goes in the v6.43.0 release notes, as previous releases have done.

commit.message:
fix(anthropic-oauth): stop a dead store masking a working credential (6.43.0)

The Claude subscription provider had never served a single request on the
reporter's machine, and four separate defects had to be fixed before it could.

B1  load_tokens() picked the managed store on has_access_token alone, so a
    file holding a token that expired days ago permanently masked a healthy
    ~/.claude credential sitting next to it. Selection is now viability-based
    (not expired, or expired with a refresh token that is not itself past its
    stated expiry) and logs one line naming the source it chose and the one it
    skipped.

B2  Every refresh failure, 429 included, was reported as "sign in again" --
    advice that rotates a working refresh token away. Failures now split into
    AnthropicOAuthRefreshRejected (400/401/403 *with* a JSON OAuth error body;
    definitive, quarantines the store) and AnthropicOAuthRefreshUnavailable
    (408/429/5xx/transport, and any 4xx whose body is not an OAuth error;
    transient, credential kept). The body check is not pedantry: the edge in
    front of the token endpoint answers a bare non-JSON 403 for reasons that
    have nothing to do with the grant.

    Per the binding decision, transient failures get no OAuth-specific retry
    loop. They are classified with the existing FailureKinds -- RATE_LIMIT,
    OVERLOADED, AUTHENTICATION, UNAVAILABLE -- and handed to the existing
    ladder, backoff, Retry-After and provider-health machinery, exactly as an
    API-key provider's 429/5xx is. No FailureKind was added.

B3  The provider read the store once and cached it for the process, so a
    dashboard import reported success while the live provider kept using the
    broken credential. It now re-resolves when the store's (mtime_ns, size)
    changes, as Claude Code does with its own file.

B4  The dashboard discarded credential_reference. Added
    fillAnthropicOAuthFields() and the "Apply settings to activate the
    provider." wording the working ChatGPT path already uses.

B5  Added POST /admin/api/anthropic-oauth/{refresh,disconnect} behind
    require_loopback_admin, with "Refresh now" and "Disconnect" buttons.
    Disconnect renames the store to anthropic_oauth.json.dead-<epoch>; nothing
    is ever deleted, and Claude Code's file is never touched.

B6  The CLI raised tracebacks. --help now exits 0 without prompting, and EOF,
    Ctrl-C and a rejected code are each one line and exit 1.

B7  The token endpoint got anthropic-beta and User-Agent: anthropic, and no
    scope. Re-derived against Claude Code 2.1.260: $U/EAn send Content-Type
    only and carry scope=p8 on refresh. anthropic-beta is dropped and scope
    added -- but a real User-Agent is kept, because a consented live test got a
    non-JSON 403 from the edge with none and a first-class OAuth answer with
    one. Every constant now cites a 2.1.260 offset and a quoted snippet.

B8  A pasted callback URL was sent to the token endpoint as the code, and the
    resulting 400 was reported as "the code was rejected, start again", which
    is wrong and loops forever. The URL, a bare query string, code#state and a
    bare code are all accepted now.

B9  Discovery logged the exception class name, so the status the exception was
    built around never reached anyone. MCC's own credential errors are marked
    safe_message and report their own text.

B10 An expired refresh token now fails viability without a network call and
    the card says so instead of showing a stale date.

Also adds the loopback callback sign-in (http://localhost:<port>/callback, an
ephemeral port on 127.0.0.1) that Claude Code itself uses, with the paste flow
as the automatic fallback where localhost means two different things; names the
macOS keychain in the import message on darwin; and pins the two OAuth
providers' failure classes together so they cannot drift apart again.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
